elements.element: Customer owns all deliverables created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The Company owns all right, title and interest in the Site, including deliverables created by HDI or for HDI under the Agreement, covering the Vendor-side deliverables produced for the Company.

elements.element: Customer owns all work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The Company expressly owns all right, title and interest in work product created by HDI or for HDI under the Agreement.

elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer all right, title and interest in the deliverables and work product.
elements.evidence: HDI expressly 'hereby assigns to the Company all right, title and interest in and to such deliverables and work product.'

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: The clause states that 'HDI shall retain ownership of its pre-existing intellectual property.'

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to Vendor intellectual property embedded in the deliverables.
elements.evidence: HDI expressly grants the Company a licence to any HDI intellectual property embedded in the deliverables.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP licence is expressly described as perpetual.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP licence is expressly described as irrevocable.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP licence is expressly described as royalty-free.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The Company retains 'all right, title and interest' in the defined Company Data.

elements.element: No intellectual property is jointly owned by the parties.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that nothing in the Agreement creates joint ownership of intellectual property.

elements.element: Vendor owns its generic tools.
elements.evidence: HDI retains only its pre-existing intellectual property. Generic tools are not identified, and newly developed generic tools could fall within the Company's broad ownership of deliverables and work product.

elements.element: Vendor owns its know-how.
elements.evidence: The clause does not expressly reserve HDI's know-how; the reservation is limited to pre-existing intellectual property.

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The Company is assigned ownership of the deliverables. The only express licence is to HDI intellectual property embedded in the deliverables, not to the deliverables themselves.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: No licence to the deliverables is granted, so there is no perpetual term applicable to such a licence.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: No licence to the deliverables is granted, so there is no irrevocability term applicable to such a licence.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: No deliverables licence is granted, and the clause contains no worldwide territorial language.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Royalty-free treatment applies only to the licence for embedded HDI intellectual property, not to a licence covering the deliverables.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to use the deliverables.
elements.evidence: There is no express deliverables licence or express licensed right to use the deliverables, notwithstanding the Company's separate ownership rights.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to modify the deliverables.
elements.evidence: No deliverables licence expressly grants a modification right.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to sublicense the deliverables.
elements.evidence: No deliverables licence expressly grants a sublicensing right.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to exercise its rights in the deliverables for Customer's business.
elements.evidence: There is no deliverables licence containing a business-use scope.

result.reason: The added section substantively satisfies every preferred requirement: Company ownership and HDI's assignment are express, HDI retains pre-existing IP while licensing embedded IP on the required terms, Company Data remains with the Company, and joint ownership is disclaimed. The fallback is not separately implemented because HDI does not expressly retain all generic tools and know-how and no licence to the deliverables with the specified scope and permissions is granted. The change is confined to the requested ownership allocation and leaves the liaison provision untouched. Drafting quality is high overall, although 'created by or for HDI' is less direct than 'created for the Company,' and the broad ownership of the Site and code would be clearer if expressly made subject to HDI's retained pre-existing IP.
